hooks.text: An asteroid gets so hot near the Sun it bakes.
The Geminid meteor shower's famous tail isn't dust.
An extreme space rock hits 750 degrees Celsius.

title: The Asteroid That Bakes Like a Comet
description: Discover how asteroid 3200 Phaethon gets close enough to the Sun to bake and create the Geminid meteor shower.

beats.text: Asteroid Phaethon orbits closer to the Sun than Mercury.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of asteroid 3200 Phaethon near the Sun, NASA, 2018
queries: Solar system asteroid near sun illustration

beats.text: Its barren rocky surface bakes up to 750 degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Carbonaceous chondrite meteorite macro specimen, laboratory, 2020

beats.text: That intense extreme heat physically cracks the rock apart.
beats.visual: Diagram of an Apollo asteroid orbit, schematic, 2019

beats.text: Scientists long thought solar dust created the annual Geminids.
beats.visual: Geminids meteor shower over landscape, long exposure night sky, 2021

beats.text: Then NASA observatories revealed the tail is actually sodium gas.
beats.visual: STEREO spacecraft model in space, NASA illustration, 2009

beats.text: Since gas cannot form meteors, the true origin remains a complete mystery.
beats.visual: DESTINY+ spacecraft JAXA illustration, concept art, 2024

beats.text: This amazing baking rock is what created the Geminids.
beats.visual: Artist concept asteroid 3200 Phaethon near sun, NASA, 2018
queries: Solar system asteroid near sun illustration

hook_text: AN ASTEROID BAKES NEAR THE SUN
